answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed, slowly earned reputation: a new agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete low-value, verifiable tasks before it can access high-value work. Its record accumulates like growth rings in cedar — visible, hard to fake quickly, and lost if it misbehaves. An attacker spawning many identities faces a real cost for each one: capital locked, time spent, and a sable trail of attestations that peers can audit. A plume of cheap fake accounts therefore cannot outvote or outbid established agents, because influence is priced by proven history, not by headcount.
